body_ar:
إن التغيير المنشود اليوم في عالمنا الإسلامي أساسه تغيير نفوس المسلمين إلى الأحسن، ولا يتم ذلك إلا بإعادة بناء الشخصية وتربيتها وتزكيتها بهذا الدين العظيم، وإن عملية بناء النفس عند الجادين المخلصين لا تعرف التوقف ولا التعثر، بل هي مستمرة عندهم حتى يأتيهم الموت، ولا تتضح معالم شخصية المسلم إلا بجهد عظيم متواصل، وبناء للنفس محكم متكامل يقوم على أسس دعا إليها الشرع وبينها.
شخصية المسلم هي التي تميزه عمن سواه:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته. أما بعد: فإن كل ملة ونحلة وكل أيديولوجية لها قيم وأسس تبينها وتميزها عما سواها، وإن هذا الدين الذي هو الدين الحق عند الله سبحانه وتعالى له ميزات هي التي تميزه عما سواه، وهي التي يزداد بها منسوب الإيمان في قلوب ذويه، وهي التي يحسن الإنسان بها إيمانه فيصبح حسن الإسلام، وبدونها ولو كان مؤمناً بقلبه ولسانه وبعض جوارحه فإن إسلامه غير حسن، وحسن الإسلام هو الذي شرطه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في تكفير الحسنات للسيئات ...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* The change sought today in our Islamic world has as its basis the changing of the souls of the Muslims for the better, and that is not accomplished except by rebuilding character, by forming it and by purifying it (tazkiyah) through this mighty religion. For the serious and the sincere, the work of building the self knows neither stopping nor stumbling; with them it continues until death comes to them. The features of the Muslim's character do not become clear except through great and continuous effort, and through a building of the self that is sound and complete and rests on foundations to which the revealed law has called and which it has set out.

## The Muslim's character is what distinguishes him from everyone else

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and God's mercy and His blessings. To proceed: every creed and every sect, and every ideology, has values and foundations that make it clear and that distinguish it from everything else. This religion — which is the true religion with God, glorified and exalted is He — has distinguishing marks: it is by them that it is distinguished from everything else; it is by them that the level of faith rises in the hearts of those who hold it; and it is by them that a person makes his faith excellent, so that he becomes excellent in his Islam. Without them — even were he a believer with his heart, his tongue and some of his limbs — his Islam is not excellent. And excellence of Islam is what the Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, made the condition for good deeds blotting out bad ones …

options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis at the moment the condition for good deeds blotting out bad ones is named, before the report behind that condition is cited and before a single feature of the character named in the title is given. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/g-21.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.arabic: وبدونها ولو كان مؤمناً بقلبه ولسانه وبعض جوارحه فإن إسلامه غير حسن، وحسن الإسلام هو الذي شرطه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في تكفير الحسنات للسيئات
flags.context: the last sentence before the text breaks off, in the Sheikh's own voice
options: his Islam is not excellent … the condition for good deeds blotting out bad ones
his Islam is not good … the requirement for good deeds to expiate bad ones
his Islam is deficient … what the Prophet stipulated for sins to be forgiven
flags.note: A statement about the standing of a Muslim's faith, and the text stops in the middle of it, which is the combination style guide section 10 exists for. The claim is graded and not exclusionary: the person described is expressly still 'a believer with his heart, his tongue and some of his limbs', and what is denied him is 'حسن الإسلام', excellence in Islam, not Islam. The English must not let 'غير حسن' slide toward 'deficient' or 'invalid', which would turn a statement about degree into a statement about membership — the single most dangerous slippage available in this passage. Note also that the condition is attributed to the Prophet ('شرطه الرسول') with no report quoted and no collection or grading given; the excerpt breaks off exactly where the report would have come. No attribution has been supplied.

'منسوب' is the level of a body of water, used here as a live metaphor for faith rising and falling. The English keeps 'level', which carries the image without labouring it, and the metaphor bears directly on the doctrine that faith admits increase and decrease — the very question flagged at record 718 of this slice.

options: every creed and every sect, and every ideology
every religion and denomination, and every ideology
every faith-community and school, and every ideology
flags.note: 'ملة' and 'نحلة' are a classical pair — the first a revealed religion as a community holds it, the second a sect or school adopted by choice — and the Sheikh sets a modern loan-word, 'أيديولوجية', alongside them. The juxtaposition is deliberate and worth keeping visible: he is putting religions and ideologies under one description in order to make a general point about what distinguishes a system. The English keeps three terms and does not harmonise the registers.

options: purifying it (tazkiyah) through this mighty religion
cultivating it by this great religion
refining it through this mighty religion
flags.note: 'تزكية' is fixed in the glossary as 'purification of the self'. It is paired here with 'تربية', formation, and 'بناء', building, and the three describe one process; the English keeps the three distinct so that the sequence the synopsis describes remains legible.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
This record and record 729 carry the same upload timestamp in their aliases, 10 May 2011 at 10:32:27; records 726 and 727 share another. The run was uploaded in batches within a few minutes.

'الشرع' is rendered 'the revealed law' rather than 'the Sharia', which in English has acquired connotations the Arabic word in this sentence does not carry; the glossary's 'مقاصد الشريعة' entry keeps 'Sharia' where the term is technical.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record. 'شرطه' in the closing sentence is the verb of 'شرط', a condition, and is treated in its own flag.
